comments.author: Alex Kim
comments.body: Bumping the buffer to 1 MiB and adding a clear error if Content-Length exceeds the cap.

content.text: Bumping the buffer to 1 MiB and adding a clear error if Content-Length exceeds the cap.

The SDK webhook verifier throws or returns invalid signature for bodies larger than 256 KiB even when the HMAC is correct. Large issue.updated payloads with big description fields fail verification every time.

Expected: any body within the platform's 1 MiB webhook cap verifies if the signature matches. Actual: the verifier reads the stream into a 256 KiB buffer and either truncates or errors before computing the digest, so the signature never matches the full body.

Hypothesis: a hard-coded maxBodyVerify = 256 << 10 in the SDK verifier predates the platform raising the webhook body limit to 1 MiB. Server-side signing uses the full body; client-side checks a prefix.
Customers with rich-text heavy projects cannot validate webhooks without a custom verifier.
